articles.title: In 2026, scientists recreated 15,000 years of solar wind exposure on Moon soil in 4 hours; the experiment could help with future lunar resource mining
articles.description: Interlune has recreated the effects of around 15,000 years of solar-wind exposure on lunar soil in just four hours, using accelerated helium ions inside a vacuum chamber. The experiment created a gas-bearing lunar soil simulant that could help companies test equipment for extracting helium-3 and other resources on Earth before sending mining technology to the Moon. The development addresses a major challenge in lunar research, where genuine Apollo soil is extremely limited and conventional simulants do not contain solar-wind gases.

articles.title: Chitrakoot Flood Update: Mandakini River Breaks 23-Year Record, Air Force Leads Rescue
articles.description: Chitrakoot is facing a severe flood situation after the Mandakini River rose dramatically and reportedly broke a 23-year water-level record. The river has been flowing above the danger mark, submerging homes, shops and large parts of the Ramghat area, while several villages have suffered extensive damage. The scale of flooding has made access to many affected locations extremely difficult, with several roads completely blocked by floodwater and debris. As residents remain stranded in vulnerable areas, rescue operations are being carried out continuously by administrative teams, with an Indian Air Force helicopter also being used to airlift people trapped by the rising waters. The latest visuals show homes surrounded or partially submerged by floodwater as the powerful current continues to flow through the affected areas. The Hanuman Dhara bridge was also swept away by the strong current, further disrupting connectivity. Authorities remain on alert and are working to move residents to safer locations. A positive development is that the water level has now started to gradually recede, although the damage left behind by the flooding remains clearly visible. Residents told reporters that the situation was among the most severe they had witnessed in decades, with comparisons being drawn to the major flooding seen in 2003. The administration and rescue teams continue to monitor the Mandakini as conditions remain challenging. With floodwater slowly declining, officials are now focusing on evacuation, relief and assessing damage in villages and urban areas that were cut off during the peak of the flooding.

articles.title: Nepal Disaster Update: Death Toll Rises to 734 as Bhotekoshi River Flood Threat Returns
articles.description: Nepal is continuing to face the devastating impact of the disaster that struck on August 26, with the reported death toll rising to 734 as rescue teams remain engaged in affected areas. Search operations are still underway to locate people who remain missing, while authorities continue to monitor flood-hit regions and changing conditions. A fresh concern has emerged along the Bhotekoshi River after Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority confirmed a sudden increase in the river’s flow. Authorities have urged people to stay away from the river and avoid vulnerable areas as the heightened water level could create additional risks for communities already affected by the disaster. Rescue and relief operations are continuing despite difficult ground conditions, with teams working to reach stranded residents and search for those still unaccounted for. The renewed rise in the Bhotekoshi River has added to concerns that another wave of flooding could affect already devastated areas. Officials are maintaining close watch on water levels and local conditions while urging residents to follow safety advisories and move to safer locations if instructed. With the death toll continuing to climb and the search for missing people still underway, Nepal remains on high alert. Authorities are expected to provide further updates as rescue teams assess the situation on the ground and determine the extent of the latest rise in the river’s flow.
